description:
Expose a public library API so per-client-crate integration tests can spawn the testjig in-process and hit it without subprocess management.

API shape (sketch — final shape TBD by claimant):

    pub fn spawn_in_process(config: TestjigConfig) -> TestjigHandle;

    pub struct TestjigConfig { /* port: 0 for random, token: default 'test-token' */ }

    pub struct TestjigHandle {
        pub addr: std::net::SocketAddr,
        pub token: String,
        // shutdown signal; drop = abort
    }

The handle's Drop impl aborts the tokio task running the server. The addr is the actual bound address (so port=0 callers get a real port back). The token is exposed so the test can build an Authorization header against it without hardcoding.

Add a smoke-test integration test in crate-jmap-testjig/tests/ that:
1. Spawns in-process at port 0
2. Builds an HTTP client (reqwest with rustls-tls)
3. Fetches /.well-known/jmap and asserts all 8 capability URIs present
4. POSTs a Core/echo via /jmap and asserts the echo
5. Drops the handle and asserts the server stops cleanly

## Acceptance

- spawn_in_process docs make clear: NOT FOR PRODUCTION
- The smoke test passes
- cargo clippy / cargo test workspace clean
- The handle type is Send + Sync so tests can move it across tokio task boundaries

## Depends on .3 (so backends are actually wired) and .6 (so auth is on the same code path tests use)
title: Integration test harness: pub fn spawn_in_process() -> (handle, addr)
